html:
A deal signed in Istanbul on 22 July 2022 that let ships carry grain from Ukraine's Black Sea ports during the war. Russia and Ukraine each signed with Turkey and the United Nations, not with each other.

After Russia invaded Ukraine, its navy blocked ports such as Odesa. Ukraine is one of the world's largest exporters of wheat, maize and sunflower oil, and the blockade pushed up food prices in poor countries that depend on imports. Under the deal, ships followed a safe corridor and were inspected near Istanbul by a joint team.

Tens of millions of tonnes of food left Ukraine this way. Russia pulled out in July 2023, saying its own exports were held back. Ukraine then opened its own route along the coast, defended by its forces. The deal showed how a war in one country can reach the dinner tables of people far away.
sum: A deal signed in Istanbul on 22 July 2022 that let ships carry grain from Ukraine's Black Sea ports during the war. Russia and Ukraine each signed with Turkey and the United Nations, not with each other.
